chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hijr ibn Za'ida, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever deliberately leaves off a single hair [unwashed] from the state of ritual impurity (janaba), then he is in the Fire.

key_terms.الجنابة: Janaba — the state of major ritual impurity requiring a full purificatory bath (ghusl al-janaba), incurred through sexual intercourse or seminal emission
key_terms.شعرة: A single hair — emphasizing the completeness required; even the tiniest omission invalidates the ghusl
key_terms.متعمداً: Deliberately/intentionally — distinguishing willful omission from accidental oversight, which is treated differently in jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What happens if someone deliberately skips washing a hair during ghusl janaba according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a stern warning that deliberately leaving even a single hair unwashed during the obligatory ritual bath (ghusl) after sexual impurity (janaba) results in eternal punishment. This ruling underscores the absolute necessity of thoroughness and intentionality in ritual purification. The harsh language reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that a valid ghusl requires complete coverage of the body — leaving any part unwashed renders the entire purification void.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from Ja`far b. Bashir from Hijr b. Za’ida from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
Whoever deliberately leaves off a single hair from [purification after] sexual impurity, then he is in the Fire.
